skill.name: monitoring-observability
skill.description: Guides setup for Prometheus metrics, alert rules, structured logging, Grafana dashboards, health checks, and observability practices.
skill.summary: Create practical monitoring foundations for applications and infrastructure.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: No malicious prompt injection, command execution intent, or credential exfiltration was found. The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, reference links, sample configuration, and documentation links. A medium privacy concern remains because the logging examples include identifiers, IP data, user agents, and stack details.

remediation.issue: Logging examples include personal identifiers and internal diagnostics.
remediation.suggestion: Use pseudonymous identifiers, redact IP addresses and user agents by default, and avoid stack traces in production logs.

remediation.issue: The metrics endpoint example does not mention access boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: State that metrics endpoints should be restricted to trusted networks or authenticated scrapers.

remediation.issue: Relative documentation links trigger path traversal scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Use marketplace skill identifiers or plain text references when publishing outside the original repository.

content.value_statement: Production systems fail silently without clear signals. This skill helps teams add metrics, logs, dashboards, alerts, and health checks with practical examples.
actual_capabilities: Shows Prometheus instrumentation for Node.js request duration and request count metrics.
Provides alert rule examples for error rate, latency, pod health, and memory usage.
Demonstrates structured Winston logging with console and file transports.
Outlines a Grafana dashboard with request, error, latency, and CPU panels.
Defines health check logic for database, Redis, and application status checks.
Summarizes golden signals for latency, traffic, errors, and saturation.
limitations: Examples need adaptation for each application stack and deployment model.
It does not install or configure monitoring tools automatically.
It does not replace security review of logs, metrics, or alert data.
Dashboard and alert examples are starter patterns, not complete SLO design.

use_cases.title: Prepare a service for production
use_cases.description: Add baseline metrics, health checks, and alerts before a new service launch.

use_cases.title: Improve incident diagnosis
use_cases.description: Create dashboards and logs that help identify latency, error, and dependency problems.

use_cases.title: Standardize team observability
use_cases.description: Use shared patterns for metrics, logging, alert thresholds, and operational runbooks.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Metrics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a web service
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add basic request metrics and a metrics endpoint to my Node.js API. Explain each metric in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Alert Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create Prometheus alert rules for high error rate, slow response time, and service downtime. Include clear thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Logging and Dashboards
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design structured logging and a Grafana dashboard for a customer-facing API. Avoid logging sensitive data.

prompt_templates.title: Review Observability Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my monitoring architecture for gaps in metrics, alerts, dashboards, health checks, and incident response workflows.

output_examples.input: Ask for production monitoring for a new API service.
output: A metrics plan covering request rate, latency, errors, and resource saturation.
Recommended alert thresholds with short descriptions and severity levels.
A dashboard outline for service health, traffic, latency, and failures.

output_examples.input: Ask for better logs during incident response.
output: A structured logging plan with timestamp, service, environment, and request context fields.
Guidance to remove secrets, personal data, and unnecessary stack traces from production logs.
A checklist for correlating logs with metrics during an incident.
A health model with healthy, degraded, and unhealthy states.
Dependency checks for database and cache systems.
Status code guidance for load balancers and orchestration platforms.

best_practices: Define service level objectives before choosing alert thresholds.
Keep metric labels low-cardinality and stable across releases.
Redact secrets and personal data before logs leave the application.
anti_patterns: Creating alerts for every warning instead of actionable user impact.
Logging full request bodies, tokens, passwords, or personal data.
Publishing metrics endpoints without network restrictions or authentication.

faq.question: What monitoring tools does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It includes patterns for Prometheus, Grafana, structured logging, health checks, and alert rules.

faq.question: Can it configure my production infrastructure automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and guidance that you must adapt and deploy with your own tooling.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this skill only for Node.js applications?
faq.answer: No. Many examples use Node.js, but the monitoring concepts apply to other application stacks.

faq.question: How should I handle sensitive data in logs?
faq.answer: Do not log secrets, passwords, tokens, full request bodies, or direct personal identifiers.

faq.question: What should I customize first?
faq.answer: Start with service objectives, critical user journeys, alert thresholds, and dashboard panels for your own system.
